reason: D4 takes vector 10 or 11 from the primary word. Python retains Capstone line instructions with a decoded size even when lowering them to exceptions.
Python static_flow can retain Capstone's coprocessor or integer mnemonic flow for a line-A or line-F primary word.
ILLEGAL and D4 BKPT are exception rows. Python assigns lengths to Capstone ILLEGAL and BKPT instruction rows.
Python static_flow falls through ILLEGAL and BKPT. Both enter vector 4.
Capstone emits MOVEC even with an unassigned EC020 control register. D4 gives vector 4 after the privilege check.
An unassigned MOVEC code cannot fall through after either privilege or control-code validation.
Capstone rejects bits in its 0xff00 word2 mask (0xfe00 for BSET). The processor reads the low byte and masks the bit index by the operand width.
Capstone requires the high immediate byte to be zero. Logic on CCR consumes the low byte and only updates CCR bits.
Capstone rejects nonzero bits 10–0 of the CMP2/CHK2 extension. The register and CHK2 selector occupy bits 15–11.
Capstone rejects the high byte of CALLM's argument-count word. The encoded count is the low byte.
Capstone rejects reserved bits of the CAS extension. The EC020 register fields are decoded independently.
Capstone applies its 0x0e38 reserved-bit mask to both CAS2 operand words. The EC020 decodes the address, compare and update register fields independently.
Capstone requires bits 10–0 of the MOVES extension to be zero. The register and direction occupy bits 15–11.
Capstone rejects bits selected by 0x83f8 in the long multiply/divide extension. Sign, width and register fields are decoded independently.
Capstone requires the unused high bit on register bitfield forms, or unused high nibble on the others, to be zero. The decoder reads the defined fields.
The final word encodes ORI.B to a data register and has no immediate word left in the image. Frozen discovery omits the entry. OCaml reports truncation.
Capstone's memory SBCD handler consumes a spurious word and prints it as an adjustment. SBCD has no extension word.
Capstone reads a long immediate operand for register BTST with immediate EA. On the EC020 the EA operand is byte-sized and occupies one word.

Capstone suppresses the outer word or long when IS and I/IS bit 2 are both set. D4 uses the low selector bits to size the displacement, including IS=1 I/IS=6 or 7. In a two-EA MOVE the missing displacement can also make Capstone read the destination extension at the wrong offset.
Python static_flow ignores the explicit condition or arithmetic exception. The OCaml graph carries both normal completion and the exception escape.
Python static_flow falls through TRAP and TRAPT. Both always raise a trap.
Python static_flow treats STOP as sequential. STOP halts pending an interrupt.
Python static_flow falls through CALLM and RTM. CALLM transfers through a module descriptor and RTM returns.
Python static_flow keeps a DBT branch edge. Its condition is always true and permits only fallthrough.
Python resolves only absolute and nonindexed PC-relative jumps/calls. Full-format direct EAs with no runtime base or index have a constant target.
Python's native label includes lowered line exceptions. The EC020 selects vector 10 or 11 directly. Example arabianmj 0x000220: fe a6.
Python's native label includes lowered ILLEGAL and BKPT exceptions. The decode disposition records vector 4. Example arabianmj 0x003160: 48 48.
Python labels lowered MOVEC with an invalid control code native. OCaml records the supervisor-mode vector 4 decode result. Example arabianmj 0x0825be: 4e 7a 00 08.
OCaml applies the EC020 24-bit bus mask to constant transfers. Python reports the full 32-bit target. Example arabianmj 0x00711a: branch to 0xfffff7a2 becomes 0xfff7a2.
OCaml registers every aligned payload offset, including interior entries and decode exceptions. Python follows only known flow from the configured RAM entry. Example pbobble3j 0x604ff0: 00 00 00 00.
T9 records a legal decode as native. Python's lower() can decline a legal instruction or addressing mode. Lowering-dependent fallback is deferred.
T9 reports statically eligible successors of legal decodes. Python suppresses every chain when lower() declines the source instruction.
The source length, exception or transfer changed under a decoder rule or the physical-address mask. The changed static chains match the reported successors.
The source successors agree but the target's decoded-entry eligibility differs due to an exception or an added total-decoder entry.
The same jump-table scan yields different executable destinations after total decoding. Cleopatr 0x0019d8 (4e bb 00 d0) loses 0x0019ca because its F-line word is vector 11.

Capstone exposes some full-format PC-indexed EAs as an address-register index mode and skips the relative scanner. Bubblemj 0x0c18b0: 4e bb 33 20 03 3c, full-format PC-based direct indexed JSR with word base displacement.
The OCaml absolute scan stops at an excluded destination. Python disassembles it during scanning and drops it only when filtering the candidate list. Landmakrj 0x0a0682: 4e bb 05 21 00 2c.

The OCaml absolute scan continues past a destination with a legal primary opcode and reserved extension bits. Capstone stops at that pointer. Bubsymphj 0x0acf50: 4e fb 35 21 00 96, destination 0x0ad038 begins 06 f5 06 f5 (CALLM count padding).

The OCaml heuristic skips pointer scans starting in the vector header. Dungeonm 0x012e46 (4e bb c9 a1 00 10) indexes through A4 and suppresses the PC base. Python treats base displacement 0x10 as an absolute table start and suggests exception handlers.

The OCaml absolute scan stops at a line exception. Capstone disassembles that word and Python treats it as an executable destination, then scans further. Pbobble4j 0x0b1884 (4e bb 05 21 00 12) points first to 0x0918a4 beginning fe 72, which takes vector 11.
